articles.title: Two Nepalis killed on Romanian railway track
articles.summary:
Two Nepalis were killed after being hit by a train in Romania’s eastern city of Bacău early Sunday morning. Their identities have not yet been disclosed.

According to a statement from the Bacău Inspectorate for Emergency Situations (ISU), the two were struck by a train at around 3:21 am while walking along the railway line near Chimiei Street.

Emergency responders, including ambulances, rescue teams and medical personnel, reached the site shortly after receiving information about the incident. They found both individuals dead upon arrival, the ISU said.

Romanian police and railway authorities have launched an investigation into the accident.

“An investigation is underway to establish how they ended up on the railway line and the circumstances that led to the accident,” the ISU said in its statement.

articles.title: Australia tightens student visa rules, rejects 64 percent of Nepali applications
articles.summary:
Australia has rejected around 64 percent of offshore student visa applications from Nepal, marking the highest rejection rate recorded for Nepali applicants, according to official data.

The surge in visa refusals comes after the Australian government tightened its screening process for international students amid concerns over migration levels, housing pressures and the integrity of the education system.

Australia categorises countries under an “Evidence Level” risk framework to determine the level of scrutiny applied during visa processing. Education sector insiders say Nepal was recently moved to “Level 3”, the highest-risk category, from “Level 2” following a government review conducted several months ago.

The impact has been most severe in the vocational education and training (VET) sector, which traditionally attracts students seeking shorter and more affordable courses. Nearly 90 percent of Nepali applications for VET courses have been rejected, with only 56 of 549 applicants receiving visas, according to recent statistics.

Around 60,000 Nepali students are currently enrolled in Australian institutions. Of them, about 56,000 are existing students, while roughly 4,000 are new arrivals.

Data from Australia’s Department of Home Affairs shows a sharp decline in new student arrivals from Nepal. Between January and May this year, only 2,700 of 7,500 offshore applicants from Nepal were granted visas. During the same period last year, 7,167 of 8,028 applicants received approvals.

The uncertainty surrounding visa approvals, combined with rising application costs, has discouraged many prospective students. Applicants currently have to pay an application fee of A$2,500 (approximately Rs260,000), which is non-refundable even if the visa is rejected.

Sanjeev Pandey, a Sydney-based lawyer, said Australia had welcomed a large number of international students after the Covid-19 pandemic, but authorities later became concerned about patterns of students changing courses and extending their stay without completing their original programmes.

“The government may have also tightened student visa rules to address growing employment and housing pressures,” Pandey said.

The stricter visa regime has raised concerns among education consultancies and smaller institutions that rely heavily on international enrolments.

Khagendra Satyal, international business development manager at Central Australian College, said the decline in student arrivals had significantly affected the sector.

“Visas are now granted only after assessing what positive contributions an international student can make to Australia in the long run,” Satyal said. “Students applying from Nepal need to understand this shift.”

The immigration crackdown also comes amid growing political pressure in Australia over migration. Analysts say the rise of politicians with hardline positions on immigration, including Pauline Hanson, has contributed to a broader political push for tighter controls.

Lawyer Pandey said the tougher environment has affected not only prospective students but also those already in Australia. Renewing student visas, switching back to student visas after completing post-study work arrangements, and bringing spouses as dependants have all become more difficult, he said.

Obtaining permanent residency has also become significantly more challenging compared with previous years.

Despite the tightening measures, Nepal remains one of the largest sources of international students in Australia. Government data shows Nepali students account for around nine percent of Australia's international student population, making Nepal the third-largest source country.

articles.title: Budget-friendly places for Nepali students in Ohio
articles.summary:
Athens is a small, scenic college town in southeastern Ohio, shaped largely by Ohio University and its energetic student community. Surrounded by rolling hills, rivers and forests, the town combines historic streets, local businesses and easy access to nature.

The university campus, downtown shops and restaurants are concentrated within a compact area, making daily life manageable without a car. Ohio University students can also use Athens Public Transit free of charge, while nearby trails and forests provide inexpensive options for hiking and outdoor recreation.

Because Athens is a relatively small town, the number of professional internships available locally can be limited. Although Ohio University hosts career fairs and attracts employers from across the country, students may need to look beyond Athens or relocate temporarily for specialised opportunities.

Oxford is a compact, classic college town in southwestern Ohio, built almost entirely around Miami University at its core. Red-brick Georgian buildings, leafy streets and a walkable uptown give it a traditional campus-town character.

The compact layout means campus, uptown restaurants, shops and student housing are all within easy walking distance. The town is also considered quite safe, and Miami University's strong sense of community brings a steady calendar of campus events, traditions and activities that keep student life active without needing to travel elsewhere.

The town's economy is heavily tied to the university, so it can feel quiet or emptied out during breaks and summer months when students are away.

ColumbusColumbus is Ohio's capital and largest city, and it's where The Ohio State University, one of the biggest campuses in the country, is situated. Rather than a self-contained college town, Columbus functions as a full city with sprawling neighborhoods, a job market, and student population that's just one part of a much bigger urban picture.

Pros:Living costs stay reasonable even with everything a major city offers, and students get real exposure to internships and employers across finance, tech, healthcare and government without having to leave town.

Cons:The scale of the city brings more traffic and scattered housing options, so building a close community takes a bit more intention than it would in a smaller town.

Cincinnati is moving to universities like the University of Cincinnati and Xavier University. The city has 300,000 people and many residential areas.

Pros:The city offers people a diverse job market. It is home to many consumer goods, finance and healthcare companies. The cost of living is on the lower end for cities of this size.

Cons:Despite its universities, the city is not generally considered a college town. Younger residents have to actively seek college-town experiences since it is not part of city life. The city is also not walkable.

Toledo is Ohio’s fourth largest city, sitting on the edge of Lake Erie. It is a city of 600,000 people and home to the University of Toledo.

Pros: The University of Toledo sits at the centre of city life. It is the biggest school in town and also the town's biggest employer. Students have a solid pipeline to work experience and internships.

Cons: As a Rust Belt city, its growth has been stagnant over the years. And despite its size, it is considered to be falling behind the other major metros in Ohio.

Based on conversations with local Nepali students in Ohio.

articles.title: Migrant workers can strike under new Qatari labour law
articles.summary:
The Qatari government has introduced a conditional right for migrant workers to stage legal strikes as part of amendments to the country’s labour law.

Under the revised law, workers can go on strike for up to six working days after notifying their employer and the Ministry of Labour in writing, but only if a labour dispute cannot be resolved through negotiation, conciliation or mediation. The provision was introduced through Qatar’s Law No 9 of 2026, which amended the 2004 Labour Law (Law No 14) to strengthen workers’ rights and welfare.

The amended law requires companies with 100 or more employees to establish joint committees made up of management and worker representatives. The committees are intended to improve workplace dialogue, strengthen consultation and help resolve disputes before they escalate.

The reforms also introduce tougher penalties for labour violations. Employers that breach wage protection regulations may face suspension of ministry services, while the Labour Dispute Resolution Committee has been formally authorised to conduct virtual hearings. Recruitment agencies and companies involved in hiring violations may face fines ranging from QAR3,000 to QAR25,000. One Qatari riyal is equivalent to Rs41.66.

Workers exercising their right to strike will not be entitled to wages during the strike period. The law also allows companies to dismiss without notice workers who organise illegal or unjustified strikes without following the required procedures or who disrupt business operations through such actions.

Companies that fail to establish mandatory joint committees may face fines ranging from QAR2,000 to QAR5,000.

Qatar has also strengthened enforcement of its Wage Protection System. The amended law gives the labour ministry greater authority to take action against employers that delay or fail to pay salaries, including suspending services, imposing administrative measures and applying regulatory penalties against repeat offenders.

If a company repeatedly violates wage rules or triggers collective disputes because of unpaid salaries, other companies under the same ownership may also face penalties. The ministry may publish the names of non-compliant companies on its website.

Workers who remain unpaid can request a change of employer or terminate their contracts, with repatriation costs to be covered by the employer.

The Labour Dispute Resolution Committee’s new authority to conduct virtual hearings means workers no longer need to be physically present to pursue labour cases. Employers, workers and verified witnesses can now participate in proceedings online.

Workers must first register disputes with the ministry. Cases are referred to the dispute resolution committee only when efforts to settle them through negotiation fail. Agreements reached through ministry-led mediation will have the status of legally enforceable documents.

The amended law also increases penalties for recruitment-related violations.

Recruitment agencies can be fined between QAR3,000 and QAR25,000 for hiring workers without ministry approval for employment contracts, processing recruitment before mandatory medical examinations or committing other administrative and recruitment-related violations.

Qatari recruitment agencies generally recruit workers in partnership with manpower agencies in Nepal, although some employers also hire directly through Nepali firms.

The new rules also require workers seeking employment in designated technical and professional occupations to obtain certificates confirming that they have completed required training and passed examinations at ministry-approved centres before starting work.

Meanwhile, Qatar has extended the non-compete period, during which an employee can be restricted from joining a competing company after leaving a job, from one year to two years. The change restores a provision that existed before 2020.

If an employee has access to sensitive client information, trade secrets or confidential company data, an employer can prevent them from joining a competitor for up to two years after the termination of employment.

The labour law amendments are aimed at modernising Qatar’s labour market, improving regulatory oversight and creating a more flexible and competitive employment system in line with the Qatar National Vision 2030. Some provisions will require additional decrees and executive regulations before they come into full effect.

“These reforms represent significant shifts that will heavily impact employers, workers, recruitment agencies and the dispute resolution system alike,” Krishna Panthi, president of the Non-Resident Nepali Association Qatar, told Kantipur.

articles.title: अमेरिकी धावक कोच डोपिङ टेस्टमा फेल, तीन वर्षको प्रतिबन्ध
articles.summary:
अमेरिकी मध्यदूरी धावक जोनाह कोचलाई रक्त डोपिङ गरेको आरोपमा तीन वर्षका लागि खेलकुदबाट प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ। अमेरिकी डोपिङ नियन्त्रण निकाय (यूएसएडीए)ले उनको ‘एथलिट बायोलोजिकल पासपोर्ट’मा असामान्य रक्त संकेत देखिएपछि डोपिङ उल्लंघन पुष्टि भएको जनाएको छ।

एथलिट बायोलोजिकल पासपोर्टमा खेलाडीको रक्तसम्बन्धी सूचकहरूलाई लामो समयसम्म निगरानी गरिन्छ। प्रत्यक्ष रूपमा प्रतिबन्धित पदार्थको परीक्षणमा नदेखिए पनि रगतमा अस्वाभाविक परिवर्तन देखिए त्यसबाट डोपिङको संकेत पहिचान गर्न सकिन्छ।

२९ वर्षीय कोचले गत वर्षको अमेरिकी आउटडोर च्याम्पियनसिपमा पुरुष १,५०० मिटर दौडमा अप्रत्याशित रूपमा स्वर्ण जितेका थिए। उनले ३ मिनेट ३०.१७ सेकेन्डको समय निकाल्दै प्रतियोगिताको कीर्तिमानसमेत बनाएका थिए। त्यस क्रममा उनले इथान स्ट्रान्ड, सन् २०२४ का ओलम्पिक स्वर्ण विजेता कोल हकरलगायतका धावकलाई पछि पारेका थिए। डोपिङ उल्लंघन पुष्टि भएपछि उनको उक्त उपाधि खोसिएको छ।

प्रतिबन्धित पदार्थ वा प्रतिबन्धित विधि प्रयोग गरेको स्वीकार गरेपछि उनलाई तीन वर्षको प्रतिबन्ध सुनाइएको यूएसएडीएले जनाएको छ। उनका सम्बन्धित प्रतिस्पर्धाका नतिजा र पुरस्कारसमेत रद्द गरिएको छ।अब उनको प्रतिबन्ध सन् २०२९ सम्म रहनेछ।

articles.title: प्रिन्स दाहाल पहिलो खेलमै पराजित
articles.summary:
नेपाल नम्बर एक खेलाडी प्रिन्स दाहाल १४औं पुष्पलाल स्मृति राष्ट्रिय वरीयता ब्याडमिन्टन प्रतियोगिताको पहिलो खेलमा नै पराजित भएका छन्।

ग्वार्कोस्थित सहआयोजक यल स्पोर्ट्स एकेडेमीको कभर्डहलमा सोमबारदेखि सुरु भएको प्रतियोगितामा समूह ‘ए’ तर्फ प्रिन्स पहिलो खेलमै पराजित भएका हुन्। एपिएफका प्रिन्स आफ्नै विभागका क्षितिज खनालसँग २-१ सेटमा पराजित भए। प्रिन्स पूर्वविश्व जुनियर नम्बर एक खेलाडी पनि हुन्।

पहिलो दिन पुरुष एकलमा शीर्ष आठ वरीयता प्राप्त खेलाडीबिच भएको खेलमा राष्ट्रिय नम्बर एक खेलाडी प्रिन्स पराजित भए। एसियन गेम्सको छनोटमा पनि प्रिन्स क्षितिजसँग नै पराजित भएका थिए। जुन हारको शृंखला पुष्पलाल स्मृति राष्ट्रिय वरीयता ब्याडमिन्टनमा पनि दोहोरिएको छ। प्रिन्सले पुनरागमन गर्ने प्रयास गरे पनि सफल भएनन्। उनले पहिलो सेट १६-२१ ले गुमाए। तर, प्रिन्सले दोस्रो सेट २१-१३ ले आफ्नो पक्षमा पारे।

तेस्रो तथा निर्णायक सेटमा पुनः १६-२१ ले पछि परेसँगै प्रिन्सले लगातार स्तब्धपूर्ण नतिजा सामना गरे। १४औं पुष्पलाल स्मृति राष्ट्रिय वरीयता ब्याडमिन्टन सोमबारबाट सुरु भएको हो। नेपाल खेलकुद महासंघको आयोजना एवं यल स्पोर्ट्स एकेडेमीको सहआयोजनामा भएको प्रतियोगिताको नेकपा एमाले संगठन प्रमुख एवं पूर्वमन्त्री भानुभक्त ढकालले उद्घाटन गरेका थिए। समूह ‘ए’ कै पुरुषको अर्को खेलमा नेपाल पुलिस क्लबका सुनील जोशीले सफलता पाए। उनले पुलिसकै जीवन आचार्यलाई १६-२१, २१-१५, २१-१५ ले हराए। समूह ‘बी’ को खेलमा आर्मीका प्रफुल महर्जनले पुलिसका दीपक बोहरालाई २१-५, २१-१७ र पिस फिटनेस सेन्टरका विष्णु कटुवालले पुलिसका देवराज रानालाई २१-१७, २१-१९ ले हराए।

महिला एकलमा समूह ‘ए’ को खेलमा पुलिसकी सुष्मा श्रेष्ठले आर्मीकी अनुमाया राईलाई २१-१६, २०-२२, २१-१६ ले हराइन्। महिलामा पनि नेपालको शीर्ष आठ वरीयतामा प्रतिस्पर्धा भएको हो। आर्मीकी रसिला महर्जनले पुलिसकी शेष्ना श्रीपालीलाई २१-८, २१-११ ले हराउँदै सुखद सुरुआत गरिन्। समूह ‘बी’ को प्रतिस्पर्धामा एपिएफकी रिहाना शेरचन र पुलिसकी निता लम्साल विजयी भए।

रिहानाले आर्मीकी अमिता गिरीलाई २१-१३, २१-१२ र निताले सिटिजन बैंककी नङ्सल तामाङलाई २१-१६, ११-२१, २१-१७ ले हराइन्। शीर्ष आठबाहेक पुरुष एकलमा कर्णालीका रमेश कामी, कस्तुरी कलेजका मिसेक छोङवाङ, आर्मीका सौर्य महर्जन र शिशिर राना, एपिएफका सुमित थोकर, आर्मीका विशाल तामाङ अन्तिम ३२ मा पुगे।

पुलिसका टोपलाल कुमाल, मन्डला ब्याडमिन्टन एकेडेमीका अनन्त पाख्रिन, आर्मीका प्रतीक विष्ट, पुलिसका जोन जसराज बालकुमारी रिमिक्सका सम्यक शाक्य, एपिएफका सुजन थापा, विनय चौधरी र सुनसरीका नरेन्द्र लिम्बु आआफ्ना प्रतिद्वन्द्वीलाई हराउँदै अन्तिम ३२ मा पुगे। नेपाल ब्याडमिन्टन संघसँग आबद्ध ६० जिल्ला, तीन विभागीय टोली आर्मी, पुलिस र एपिएफ का ४८२ खेलाडीले १५ विधामा प्रतिस्पर्धा गर्दै छन्।

आगामी साउन ३० गतेसम्म आयोजना हुने प्रतियोगितामा ब्याडमिन्टनका शीर्ष आठ वरीयताका महिला/पुरुष एकल, शीर्ष आठ वरीयताबाहेक महिला/पुरुष एकल, महिला/पुरुष युगल खुला, यु-११, यु-१५ र यु-१९ छात्र तथा छात्रा खुला एकल, ३५ वर्ष माथिको खुला युगल, ४५ र ५५ वर्षमाथि मास्टर्स खुला युगल गरि १५ विधामा प्रतिस्पर्धा हुनेछ।

प्रतियोगितामा ४५ र ५५ वर्षमाथि मास्टर्स खुला युगलतर्फ विदेशी खेलाडीहरूले पनि सहभागिता जनाउने र त्यसका लागि विदेशी खेलाडीलाई आमन्त्रण गरी सकिएको महासचिव सुनीलमान शाक्यले बताए। प्रतियोगितामा लगातार तीन संस्करणमा जित हात पार्ने खेलाडीले मोटरसाइकल/स्कुटर प्राप्त गर्नेछन्। यसअघि लगातार तीन संस्करण जितेका प्रिन्सले मोटरसाइकल प्राप्त गरेका थिए।

शीर्ष आठ वरीयता प्राप्त महिला तथा पुरुषका खेल लिग कम नकआउटका आधारमा हुनेछन्। शीर्ष आठका खेलाडीलाई दुई समूहमा विभाजन गरिनेछ। समूहबाट शीर्ष दुई स्थान प्राप्त गर्ने खेलाडी सेमिफाइनलमा प्रवेश गर्नेछन्। विजेताले नगद ५० हजार, उपविजेताले नगद ३५ हजार, तेस्रो हुने खेलाडीले १५ हजार प्राप्त गर्नेछन्।

articles.title: माग बढेसँगै अण्डाको समर्थन मूल्य बढ्यो
articles.summary:
अण्डाको माग बढेपछि व्यवसायीले समर्थन मूल्य बढाएका छन्। नेपाल लेयर्स कुखुरापालक सङ्घले आजदेखि लागू हुने गरी अण्डाको समर्थन मूल्य बढाएको हो।

सङ्घका अनुसार एक्सएल अण्डा प्रतिक्रेट (३० वटाको) रु ५६०, ठूलो अण्डा रु ५४५, मिडियम रु ५०० र सानो रु तीन हजार प्रतिपेटी (सात क्रेट) समर्थन मूल्य कायम गरिएको हो। सङ्घका अध्यक्ष विनोद पोखरेलका अनुसार बर्डफ्लुको सङ्क्रमण हटेको र धेरै कुखुरा मरेसँगै उत्पादन घटेकाले बजारको माग निकै बढेको छ।

माग बढेसँगै अण्डाको मूल्य बढेको हो। फार्महरुले दिएको रेटका आधारमा समर्थन मूल्य जारी गरिएको उनले बताए। मूल्य बढ्दै गर्दा पनि किसानले लागत मूल्य पाउन नसकेको उनले बताए। अण्डाको लागत मूल्य प्रतिगोटा रु १९.१२ पर्न आउँछ। यसलाई हिसाब गर्दा प्रतिक्रेट रु ५७३.६ हुन आउँछ।

बर्डफ्लुका कारण किसानले ठूलो क्षति व्यहोर्नु परेको छ। लागत मूल्य पाउन नसकेपछि विगत केही वर्षदेखि किसान यस पेसाबाट पलायन हुन थालेका छन्। पछिल्लो समय उत्पादन घट्नु, कुखुरामा रोग लग्नुलगायत कारणले किसान बैंकको ऋणको भरमा पर्दै आएको व्यवसायी बताउँछन्। पछिल्लो समय बर्डफ्लुका कारण केही किसानको कुखुरा मरेका थिए भने कुखुरा हुनेहरुले अण्डाको मूल्य नपाउँदा ठूलो नोक्सानी व्यहोर्नु परेको पोखरेलले बताए।

articles.title: छोटी भन्सार पुनःसञ्चालनको माग
articles.summary:
कैलालीको पृथ्वीपुर छोटी भन्सार कार्यालय पुनःसञ्चालन तथा स्तरोन्नतिको माग गर्दै सोमबार अर्थमन्त्री डा स्वर्णिम वाग्लेलाई ज्ञापनपत्र बुझाइएको छ।

कैलालीका सात स्थानीय तहका जनप्रतिनिधि र भजनी उद्योग वाणिज्य सङ्घले संयुक्त रूपमा ज्ञापनपत्र बुझाउँदै लामो समयदेखि बन्द रहेको भजनी नगरपालिका–५ लालबोझीस्थित पृथ्वीपुर छोटी भन्सार कार्यालय तत्काल पुनःसञ्चालन गर्न माग गरेका हुन्। विसं २०२२ देखि सञ्चालनमा रहेको पृथ्वीपुर भन्सार कार्यालयलाई सरकारको निर्णयअनुसार बन्द गरिएपछि स्थानीयवासीले असन्तुष्टि व्यक्त गर्दै आएका छन्।

लामो समयदेखि सञ्चालनमा रहेको सो भन्सार कार्यालय हटाइएपछि हाल सेवा अवरुद्ध भएको र यसबाट स्थानीय नागरिकले समस्या भोग्नुपरेको जनाइएको छ। भन्सार कार्यालय बन्द हुँदा कैलाली जिल्लाका सम्बन्धित स्थानीय तहका तीन लाखभन्दा बढी नागरिक, कृषक, व्यापारी तथा उद्योगीलाई ठूलो सास्ती भइरहेको ज्ञापनपत्रमा उल्लेख छ। भन्सार कार्यालय पुनःसञ्चालनका लागि भजनी नगरपालिकाले यसअघि नै भन्सार विभाग, त्रिपुरेश्वरमा पत्राचार गरिसकेको ज्ञापनपत्रमा उल्लेख गरिएको छ।

सो भन्सार कार्यालयले भजनी, घोडाघोडी र गौरीगङ्गा नगरपालिका तथा जोशीपुर, बर्दगोरिया, कैलारी र जानकी गाउँपालिकाका तीन लाखभन्दा बढी नागरिक, व्यापारी, उद्योगी तथा कृषकलाई सेवा प्रदान गर्दै आएको छ । साथै, कार्यालयले राजस्व सङ्कलन वृद्धि तथा राजस्व चुहावट नियन्त्रणमा महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पुर्‍याउँदै आएको ज्ञापनपत्रमा उल्लेख छ ।

articles.title: अमेरिकी धावक कोच डोपिङ टेस्टमा फेल, तीन वर्षको प्रतिबन्ध
articles.summary:
अमेरिकी मध्यदूरी धावक जोनाह कोचलाई रक्त डोपिङ गरेको आरोपमा तीन वर्षका लागि खेलकुदबाट प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ। अमेरिकी डोपिङ नियन्त्रण निकाय (यूएसएडीए)ले उनको ‘एथलिट बायोलोजिकल पासपोर्ट’मा असामान्य रक्त संकेत देखिएपछि डोपिङ उल्लंघन पुष्टि भएको जनाएको छ।

एथलिट बायोलोजिकल पासपोर्टमा खेलाडीको रक्तसम्बन्धी सूचकहरूलाई लामो समयसम्म निगरानी गरिन्छ। प्रत्यक्ष रूपमा प्रतिबन्धित पदार्थको परीक्षणमा नदेखिए पनि रगतमा अस्वाभाविक परिवर्तन देखिए त्यसबाट डोपिङको संकेत पहिचान गर्न सकिन्छ।

२९ वर्षीय कोचले गत वर्षको अमेरिकी आउटडोर च्याम्पियनसिपमा पुरुष १,५०० मिटर दौडमा अप्रत्याशित रूपमा स्वर्ण जितेका थिए। उनले ३ मिनेट ३०.१७ सेकेन्डको समय निकाल्दै प्रतियोगिताको कीर्तिमानसमेत बनाएका थिए। त्यस क्रममा उनले इथान स्ट्रान्ड, सन् २०२४ का ओलम्पिक स्वर्ण विजेता कोल हकरलगायतका धावकलाई पछि पारेका थिए। डोपिङ उल्लंघन पुष्टि भएपछि उनको उक्त उपाधि खोसिएको छ।

प्रतिबन्धित पदार्थ वा प्रतिबन्धित विधि प्रयोग गरेको स्वीकार गरेपछि उनलाई तीन वर्षको प्रतिबन्ध सुनाइएको यूएसएडीएले जनाएको छ। उनका सम्बन्धित प्रतिस्पर्धाका नतिजा र पुरस्कारसमेत रद्द गरिएको छ।अब उनको प्रतिबन्ध सन् २०२९ सम्म रहनेछ।

articles.title: India, China invite PM Shah to visit as he opens up diplomatic engagement
articles.summary:
The ambassadors of India and China on Monday invited Prime Minister Balendra Shah to visit their respective countries as they separately met with him in Kathmandu within a few hours of each other.

Indian Ambassador Naveen Srivastava reminded Shah of the invitation extended by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to visit India, while Chinese Ambassador Zhang Maoming also invited the prime minister to China. Shah acknowledged both invitations but did not commit to any visit or indicate possible dates, according to officials familiar with the meetings.

“Since I am retiring at the end of September, it would be a great pleasure if you visit India by then,” Srivastava reportedly told Shah.

In response, the prime minister said that he would visit India at an appropriate time. Shah also stated that his government is ready to remove any obstacles on India-funded projects in Nepal and asked Ambassador Srivastava about any shortcomings. The prime minister and the Indian ambassador also briefly discussed some future projects, including Janakpur-Ayodhya rail to Buddhist circuit.

According to one official, the Indian ambassador briefed some obstacles that Indian companies have faced in Nepal.

The back-to-back meetings, held after four and a half months of Shah’s premiership, signal that his government is beginning to move away from his earlier policy of limiting individual diplomatic engagements and is seeking to maintain balanced relations with Nepal’s two immediate neighbours.

Shah met Srivastava and Zhang separately on Monday, with the meetings taking place only a few hours apart. Both ambassadors were accompanied by senior officials from their respective embassies.

The meetings were the first individual courtesy calls between Shah and the Kathmandu-based ambassadors of India and China since he became prime minister on March 27.

The decision to meet the ambassadors of Nepal’s two immediate neighbours on the same day appears intended to underscore their equal importance to Nepal, although the scheduling broadly retains the government’s stated foreign policy priority of engaging India first, followed by China.

The meetings also marked a break from Shah’s self-imposed moratorium on individual meetings with foreign diplomats immediately after taking office. Instead, he had held joint meetings with Kathmandu-based ambassadors on April 9 and May 26.

Monday’s meetings suggest that Shah has now opened up his engagement with both domestic stakeholders and foreign representatives.

Following his meeting with Shah, Indian Ambassador Srivastava said on X that he had conveyed Prime Minister Modi’s warm greetings and had an “engaging and productive exchange of views” on further deepening the “robust, multi-faceted Nepal-India partnership”.

A statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office said Srivastava congratulated Shah and expressed his commitment to further strengthening mutual relations and cooperation between the two countries. Shah, in turn, emphasised the need to further deepen Nepal’s historic relations with India and work together in areas of common interest.

The Chinese Embassy, in a readout posted on its WeChat account, said Shah told Ambassador Zhang that Nepal attaches great importance to its traditional friendship with China and is willing to work with Beijing to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation in various fields and further advance bilateral relations.

The two sides discussed issues related to Nepal-China bilateral friendship, mutual interests, development partnership and cooperation, according to the readout.

The Chinese ambassador also reiterated the invitation sent to Prime Minister Shah by his Chinese counterpart Li Qiang. The prime minister stated that he will visit China at an appropriate time.

While thanking Shah for continuously upholding the one-China policy, the Chinese ambassador also urged him to look after China’s sensitivities. The Chinese side raised the usual concerns that they used to raise on other occasions, the official added.

“Zhang congratulated Shah on the achievements made since he assumed office as Prime Minister of Nepal and reaffirmed China’s firm support for Nepal,” the Chinese Embassy said. Zhang also expressed China’s willingness to work with Nepal to implement important understandings reached by the leaders of the two countries and deepen the strategic cooperative partnership between Nepal and China.

The prime minister spoke for hardly five minutes to both ambassadors. Most of the time, the prime minister listened to them, the official added.

Former Major General Binoj Basnyat said Shah’s meetings with the Indian and Chinese ambassadors represented a timely shift from a position of avoidance to one of engagement.

“The recognition that immediate neighbours are a diplomatic priority is important,” Basnyat told the Post. “The test now is what those engagements deliver—investment, connectivity, energy, trade, technology, development and security cooperation.”

Diplomacy, he added, must ultimately convert engagement into the concrete advancement of Nepal’s national interests.

articles.title: Shah government formed commissions but cares little for the outcome
articles.summary:
Forming high-level probe commissions and task forces in response to public outrage is a long-standing political practice in Nepal. For decades, governments have responded to crises by setting up investigative panels, often to address public anger.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s government came to power promising to break with such practices and usher in greater transparency and accountability.

Yet months into its tenure, the administration appears to be repeating the pattern it had pledged to change.

A review by Kantipur shows that the Shah-led government has formed at least 10 high-profile commissions and investigative committees since taking office. But the urgency shown in forming them appears to disappear once they complete their work and submit their reports.

Reports on constitutional reform, national security, human rights violations and loss of life have either not been made public, not been formally received or remain unimplemented. The practice has raised questions over the purpose and effectiveness of commissions that are established at considerable public expense.

One of the clearest examples is the debate paper on constitutional amendment.

Amid widespread political dissatisfaction, the Cabinet decided on March 30 to form a specialised task force to prepare a comprehensive paper on possible constitutional amendments.

Coordinated by Prime Minister Shah’s political adviser, Asim Shah, the task force began work on April 8. After consultations with political parties, legal experts and civic stakeholders, it completed its assignment and submitted its final report to the government on July 16.

According to people familiar with the document, the task force proposed sweeping constitutional changes. The debate paper reportedly recommends amendments to 242 articles of the constitution and calls for the formation of a high-level constitution amendment commission to oversee the process.

Despite the scale of the proposed changes, the report remains with the prime minister’s office. The government has neither made it public nor initiated broader parliamentary or public discussion on its recommendations.

Sources say the government has hesitated to release the report because opposition parties and some smaller political groups have declined to take ownership of it.

Constitutional experts, however, say political disagreement does not absolve the government of its responsibility to make the report public. After spending state resources and months collecting suggestions, they argue that the government should release the debate paper and allow a national discussion on the proposed changes.

By keeping it out of the public domain, the prime minister’s office has stalled debate on potentially far-reaching changes to the country’s constitutional framework.

Legal experts and former government officials see the handling of commissions as more than an administrative lapse. They say it reflects a long-standing political practice in which governments establish panels to ease immediate pressure without addressing the underlying causes of a crisis.

Former high court judge Lokendra Mallik said successive governments had fallen into this pattern.

“To address immediate problems and release political stress, governments form commissions. But they are plagued by a common disease of never implementing them,” Mallik said. “In the past as well, numerous such commissions and committees were formed. Nobody knows where their reports are today. Unfortunately, the same tendency is visibly repeating itself in the current government.”

Former law minister Govinda Bandi was more critical of the Rastriya Swatantra Party government’s reliance on probe panels. He said commissions in Nepal have increasingly become tools for diverting public attention and providing political patronage.

“In Nepal, commissions have become little more than vehicles for providing positions to politically connected individuals,” Bandi said. “Because this practice has persisted for years, their reports are rarely made public or acted upon. That is why the public must ask why these commissions and probe committees are formed in the first place.”

Bandi said judicial and non-judicial probe committees are generally formed when regular state investigations fail to establish the truth or when victims have legitimate concerns about police investigations.

“A probe commission is formed to uncover the absolute truth and to ensure that such tragic incidents do not repeat in the future,” Bandi said. “The fundamental purpose is to amend laws, reform policies, and improve state institutions based strictly on the commission’s recommendations.”

Instead, he said, commissions are increasingly being used to divert public attention.

“Nothing productive has come out of this mechanism. The current government urgently needs to reflect upon and learn from this failure,” Bandi said.

The Shah administration’s selective approach to accountability is evident in its handling of reports on the Gen Z protests of September 8 and 9 last year.

To investigate the protests and the state’s response, the previous government led by Sushila Karki formed a high-level probe commission on September 21, 2025, under former judge Gauri Bahadur Karki. The commission submitted its report on March 8 earlier this year.

The responsibility for implementing the report fell to the Balendra Shah government. At its first Cabinet meeting on March 27, the government decided to implement the commission’s report. The following day, authorities arrested former prime minister KP Sharma Oli and former home minister Ramesh Lekhak over their roles in the events of September 8.

But implementation of the Karki commission’s report has stalled. The government has been accused of selectively using the report for political retribution while failing to address the loss of life and destruction of property during the September 9 violence.

Gauri Bahadur Karki, chair of the commission formed to investigate the September 8-9 incidents, said the government must explain why their report remains unimplemented.

“We worked diligently to uncover the facts and provided recommendations to prevent future crises, but I have no idea why they are not being implemented,” Karki said. “In the past, the failure to implement reports on cooperatives and medical education meant that those exact problems have resurfaced today. Because this report contains vital institutional recommendations, it would be in the nation’s interest to implement it fully.”

Karki, who previously served on the commission looking into predatory lending practices, said the failure to implement past recommendations had contributed to the recurrence of similar problems. Victims of loan-sharking marched in Kathmandu again just days ago, he noted.

“Governments do not study the commission’s suggestions, nor do they implement them,” Karki said. “Recommendations and suggestions are given specifically for implementation. In the Gen Z incident, there were many systemic issues that needed addressing, but the government does not seem to be in the mindset to execute them.”

On September 9, the commission recommended further police investigation because photographs alone were insufficient to establish individual responsibility. The government has not formed the recommended follow-up committee.

Government spokesperson Sasmit Pokhrel said the September 9 events required “consultations with political parties” before administrative action could be finalised.

A separate report by the National Human Rights Commission on the Gen Z protests also remains at the Prime Minister’s Office. An NHRC committee led by member Lily Thapa made detailed recommendations on human rights violations on September 8 and 9 last year. The government has neither taken the recommendations to the Cabinet for endorsement nor indicated that it plans to revisit the investigations.

The government’s handling of the Gen Z reports has also left questions over the conduct of security personnel unresolved.

When the Cabinet decided on March 27 to implement parts of the Gauri Bahadur Karki report, it acknowledged that the original commission had not adequately examined the internal dynamics and failures of the security apparatus during the protests.

The Cabinet therefore decided to form a separate three-member committee to investigate the conduct of security personnel. Former judge Prem Raj Karki was appointed its coordinator on April 15, with the committee given a month to complete its work.

The committee sought and received a short extension, saying the initial time provision was insufficient. It subsequently completed its investigation.

But the home ministry refused to formally receive the report.

On July 9, committee members led by Karki went to the home ministry to submit their findings. They met senior ministry officials, including the home secretary. During the meeting, Home Minister Sudan Gurung said he would not accept the report at that time and directed the committee to submit it to Prime Minister Shah instead.

The committee has since been unable to secure an appointment with the prime minister.

On August 6, its members went to the prime minister’s office and met chief secretary Govinda Bahadur Karki. According to a committee member, the chief secretary said he would “create an environment” for the report to be received in the coming days.

Until then, the committee’s assessment of the security agencies’ conduct during the protests remains in limbo.

Beyond political and constitutional issues, the government’s failure to act on probe reports has left families of victims of tragedies waiting for answers and justice.

On July 9, Ganesh Nepali (Bishwakarma) attempted self-immolation after dousing himself in petrol outside the Department of Passports in Tripureshwar. The incident followed a dispute over a parking fine imposed by the Kathmandu Metropolitan City police. Nepali succumbed to injuries later while undergoing treatment.

His family blamed harassment by the KMC police for his death and initially refused to claim his body. To defuse the tension, the government agreed to address the family’s demands and formed a probe committee on July 22 led by former judge Keshav Prasad Bastola.

The Bastola committee completed its investigation and submitted a report to the government on August 3. A week later, however, the Cabinet had neither discussed the report nor begun the process of making its findings public, leaving the bereaved family waiting for answers.

A similar situation has emerged in eastern Nepal. Following a serious incident in Kaptanganj, Sunsari, on the night of July 26, the home ministry formed a seven-member study committee led by joint secretary Bhupendra Thapa.

Given one week to complete its work, the committee travelled to Kaptanganj, questioned witnesses, consulted local residents and security agencies, and prepared its report.

Despite the urgency, the government has yet to formally receive the document. According to a committee member, the home minister has repeatedly failed to make time to accept the findings.

The report, which requires immediate implementation to maintain local law and order, now sits in a committee member’s personal drawer.

The government’s inaction contrasts with its own commitments. Point 8 of its 100-day action plan acknowledged the long-standing practice of leaving commission reports in archives. It promised that within 30 days of receiving any commission report, the government would initiate the necessary legal, administrative and prosecutorial procedures for implementation.

Point 7 of the agenda promised to form a high-level committee within a week to investigate the September 9 incident. Both commitments were ratified at the first Cabinet meeting on March 27.

The government has sought to project transparency by declassifying several old investigative reports from previous administrations, including those concerning the Tribhuvan University’s land, Bal Mandir properties and the Rawal Commission on public land. But reports generated during its own tenure have remained largely inaccessible.

Asked by Kantipur about the failure to implement the findings, Home Minister Gurung said reports and committee findings received by the government were “under study” and would be made public in due course.

The government is also sitting on the investigative report concerning anomalies and serious errors in the Grade 12 examination results, as well as the probe into the recent Siraha and Saptari incidents.

Even active commissions have been paralysed.

The property investigation commission, established by the Shah administration to investigate the assets of public officials, has been effectively halted by an interim Supreme Court order. Unable to proceed with its investigation, the commission has merely opened bundles of property declarations submitted to its office.

The government’s list of investigative bodies includes the Gen Z probe, the NHRC recommendations, the Home Minister Gurung probe, the probe on security personnel’s role on Gen Z protests, the Ganesh Nepali self-immolation probe, the property investigation commission, the constitution amendment task force, the Grade 12 error committee, the Siraha/Saptari incident commission and the cooperatives probe.It is nothing new for successive governments to shelve investigation reports. Whether it was the Property Investigation Commission formed under the chairmanship of then Supreme Court Justice Bhairab Lamsal, or the Mallik and Raymajhi commissions formed to investigate repression during the 1990 and 2006 people’s movements, successive governments have largely ignored their findings. None of these reports was either made public or fully implemented.

During the 1990 movement against the Panchayat system, 45 people were killed and around 500 injured. The government subsequently formed a commission under the chairmanship of Justice Janardan Mallik to investigate the violence. The commission recommended action against those responsible for the repression. Its recommendations, however, were never fully implemented.

During the second People’s Movement in 2006, 26 people were killed and more than 4,000 injured. In April that year, the government formed an inquiry commission under former Supreme Court Justice Krishna Jung Raymajhi. The commission recommended action against those who led the government at the time and those involved in the repression of protesters. The report, too, remains largely unaddressed.

This pattern has extended beyond political movements and state repression. Successive governments have formed commissions and committees to investigate irregularities, corruption, smuggling and administrative failures, only to leave their reports gathering dust.

In 2015, as preparations were underway to promulgate the new constitution, violence in Tikapur, Kailali, left several people dead. In September 2016, the government formed an investigation commission under former Supreme Court Justice Girish Chandra Lal. Although the commission submitted its report, it has yet to be made public.

In March 2017, five people were killed when security forces opened fire during a protest in Malleth, Saptari. The investigation report into the incident also remains confidential.

In March 2018, after a 33-kg gold smuggling case came to light, the government formed an investigation committee under the leadership of Ishwar Raj Poudel. The committee submitted its report, but its findings were not acted upon. Years later, when a 61-kg gold smuggling case emerged, the government formed another investigation committee under former Justice Dilli Raj Acharya. That committee was reportedly not even given access to the earlier Poudel-led committee’s report.

The government’s reluctance to act on such findings is not limited to irregularities and smuggling cases. Reports on administrative and ministerial reforms have met a similar fate. Reports prepared under the leadership of economist Achyut Wagle, former Chief Secretary Leelamani Poudel, legal expert Kashiraj Dahal and Laxman Aryal remain unaddressed.

The same is true of investigations into the encroachment of public and trust land. The government has yet to implement the report prepared under the leadership of former Justice Mohan Raman Bhattarai. Likewise, the report of the commission formed in September 2023 under former judge Baburam Regmi to investigate irregularities at the Social Welfare Council has not been implemented.

Similarly, the report on institutional reform prepared under the leadership of former Finance Secretary Shankar Prasad Adhikari has yet to be made public. Other investigation reports, including the one concerning the Biratnagar Jute Mill, have also remained either unpublished or unimplemented.

The recurring pattern is clear: governments form commissions in response to public pressure, allow them to investigate and submit reports, and then often keep their findings out of the public domain or fail to act on their recommendations.

articles.title: बजेट पेस गर्न नसकेका चार नगरपालिकामा सहसचिव नेतृत्वको टोली जाँदै
articles.summary:
भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी, संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासन मन्त्रालयले चालु आर्थिक वर्षका लागि स्थानीय तहको सभामा बजेट पेस गर्न नसकेका मधेस प्रदेशका केही नगरपालिकामा पुनः स्थलगत सहजीकरण गर्ने भएको छ।

सहजीकरणका लागि मन्त्रालयका सहसचिवको नेतृत्वमा प्रधानमन्त्री तथा मन्त्रिपरिषद्को कार्यालय, राष्ट्रिय सतर्कता केन्द्र तथा नेपाल नगरपालिका संघका अध्यक्षलगायतका प्रतिनिधिको संयुक्त टोली सम्बन्धित नगरपालिकामा स्थलगत रूपमा जाने कार्यक्रम तय भएको मन्त्रालयले जनाएको छ।

मन्त्रालयका अनुसार विभिन्न पहल, प्रयास तथा समन्वयमार्फत बजेट पेश गर्ने वातावरण बनाउन खोजिए पनि हालसम्म नगरसभामा बजेट पेस हुन नसकेका स्थानीय तहमा उक्त टोली जान लागेको हो।

टोलीले धनुषाको कमला नगरपालिका तथा रौतहटका गरुडा नगरपालिका, फतुवा विजयपुर नगरपालिका र मौलापुर नगरपालिका पुगेर स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि, कर्मचारी तथा सरोकारवालासँग प्रत्यक्ष छलफल गर्नेछ। बजेट निर्माण तथा नगरसभा सञ्चालनमा देखिएका समस्या पहिचान गर्दै आवश्यक सहजीकरण र समन्वय गर्ने मन्त्रालयले जनाएको छ।

स्थानीय तहको बजेट प्रक्रिया लामो समयसम्म अवरुद्ध हुँदा सेवा प्रवाह तथा विकास निर्माणका काम प्रभावित हुन सक्ने भएकाले समस्या समाधानका लागि मन्त्रालयले स्थलगत रूपमा नै सहजीकरण गर्न लागेको हो।

मन्त्रालयले स्थानीय तहमा देखिएका बजेट तथा सभा सञ्चालनसम्बन्धी समस्या समाधानका लागि आवश्यक समन्वय र सहजीकरणलाई निरन्तरता दिइरहेको छ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्ण पर्व मनाइँदै
articles.summary:
सांस्कृतिक परम्पराअनुसार आज घण्टाकर्ण पर्व मनाइँदै छ। श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन मनाइने यस पर्वलाई गठामङ्गल पनि भनिन्छ।

परापूर्वकालदेखि नेवार समुदायल मनाउँदै आएको यस पर्वमा गठामङ्गल नाम गरेको नरभक्षी राक्षस मारिएको सम्झनास्वरूप आज हरियो नर्कट, निगालो अथवा गहुँको छ्वाली मिसाएर तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको स्वरूप बनाई दोबाटो र चौबाटोमा उभ्याइने चलन छ। पर्वको तयारीका लागि आज बिहानै स्नान, घर–आँगन सफा गरी पूजापाठ गरिन्छ।

केटाकेटीले बाटामा डोरी टाँगेर पैसा (जगात्) माग्ने र राति राँको बाली गठामङ्गल नामक राक्षसको प्रतीकलाई घिसार्दै जलाइन्छ। गोपाल वंशावलीअनुसार गठामङ्गललाई सत्य, रज र तम गुण मानेर भैरवका प्रतीकका रूपमा लिइने र नवविवाहित स्त्री–पुरुषले दर्शन गर्नुपर्ने परम्परा नेवार समुदायमा रहेको इतिहास एवं संस्कृतिविद् प्रकाश श्रेष्ठ ‘सक्व’ले बताए।

जीवनमा बाध्य बाधा, आन्तरिक बाधा एवं शत्रुबाट रक्षा प्राप्त गर्नुका साथै आर्थिक र भौतिक उन्नतिका लागि घण्टाकर्णको पूजा आराधना कार्यलाई महत्वपूर्ण मानिन्छ।

articles.title: भागिरथ चलाउनेको तीज गीत ‘को मुर्खले लान्छ र मलाई’ सार्वजनिक
articles.summary:
हरितालिका तीज नजिकिएसँगै कलाकार तथा सर्जकहरू नयाँ तीज गीत रेकर्डिङ तथा भिडियो निर्माणमा व्यस्त छन्। यही क्रममा चर्चित लोक तथा दोहोरी गायक भागिरथ चलाउनेको नयाँ तीज गीत ‘को मुर्खले लान्छ र मलाई’ सार्वजनिक भएको छ।

भागिरथ चलाउने र सरिता सुनारको स्वरमा रहेको उक्त गीत हिजोमात्रै युट्युबमार्फत सार्वजनिक गरिएको हो। गीतमा जलन विश्वकर्माको शब्द तथा भागिरथ चलाउनेकै संगीत रहेको छ भने विनोद बाजुरालीले संगीत संयोजन गरेका छन्।

गीतको मिक्सिङ तथा मास्टरिङ खडक बाजुराली, भोकल सम्पादन राजेन्द्र बाजुराली र रेकर्डिङ सागर बाजुरालीले गरेका छन्। गीतको रेकर्डिङ मालाश्री स्टुडियोमा गरिएको हो।

गीतको भिडियोमा भागिरथ चलाउने र करिश्मा ढकालको अभिनय देख्न सकिन्छ। भिडियोको छायांकन अजय रेग्मीको टिमले गरेको हो भने लक्ष्मण चौहानले सम्पादन गरेका छन्।

गायक चलाउनेका यसअघि पनि थुप्रै तीज गीत सार्वजनिक भइसकेका छन्। ‘झमझम झम्काना’, ‘थोपडाले धोका दियो बरिलै’, ‘मायाले त होला’ र ‘मेरा लागि मर्ने केटो मनै परेन’ लगायतका गीतले दर्शक तथा श्रोतामाझ राम्रो चर्चा र लोकप्रियता पाएका छन्।

चलाउनेले यस वर्ष सार्वजनिक गरेको ‘को मुर्खले लान्छ र मलाई’ गीतले पनि श्रोता तथा दर्शकबाट राम्रो प्रतिक्रिया पाइरहेको बताए।

articles.title: LPG imports are up. Why are consumers still queuing for it?
articles.summary:
Nepal’s imports of liquefied petroleum gas have not fallen. Government officials and industry representatives say imports have actually increased in recent weeks.

Yet cooking gas remains difficult to find in the market, with consumers queuing for hours with empty cylinders.

For about four months, Nepal sold only half-filled cylinders to ease pressure on supplies after tensions in West Asia raised concerns about possible disruptions. That reduced apparent demand.

But when full 14.2-kilogram cylinders went back on sale, pent-up demand returned almost overnight. Shortages quickly reappeared.

So where is the gas getting stuck?

The problem is not simply a lack of imports. It lies deeper in Nepal’s supply chain, including the management of cylinders, storage capacity, distribution and transport.

Here is what is happening.

When did the shortage begin, and why?

Pressure on Nepal’s LPG supply began in February as tensions escalated in West Asia.

Fearing that the war involving the United States, Israel and Iran could disrupt supplies, Nepal Oil Corporation, the state-owned fuel supplier, decided on March 13 to sell only half-filled LPG cylinders, containing 7.1 kilograms instead of the usual 14.2 kilograms.

The arrangement continued for about four months.

Selling half-filled cylinders reduced consumption and eased immediate pressure on the market. With consumers buying less gas, the supply system was able to cope despite concerns over imports.

As supply from India stabilised, the corporation resumed sales of full 14.2-kilogram cylinders on July 15.

That immediately pushed demand higher. The shortage returned.

Has Nepal been receiving less gas from India?

Nepal Oil Corporation's figures do not show a sustained fall in LPG imports.

In February, when concerns over the West Asian conflict first intensified, Nepal sold 51,192 tonnes of LPG. By August 8, it had already imported 41,294 tonnes in the current Nepali month, according to Nagendra Sah, NOC managing director.

Sah says supplies are currently regular.

Imports during the final four Nepali months of the previous fiscal year were also substantial. Nepal imported 48,327 tonnes in mid-March to mid-April, 46,503 tonnes in mid-April to mid-May, 49,816 tonnes in mid-May to mid-June and 47,933 tonnes in mid-June to mid-July.

Gas industry representatives say imports have not fallen. Industry operator Shiva Ghimire estimates they have increased by between 15 and 25 percent recently.

The evidence therefore points away from a simple import shortage.

The bigger problem is what happens to the gas after it enters Nepal.

If there is enough gas, why are consumers still queuing?

The return to full-cylinder sales created a sudden surge in demand.

For four months, households had been buying only half the usual quantity. Once full cylinders became available again, that suppressed demand came back at once.

According to Sah, complaints were limited while half-filled cylinders were being sold. The situation changed when full cylinders returned to the market.

Large numbers of empty cylinders also came back into circulation, putting additional pressure on the distribution system.

But the problem goes beyond the sudden increase in demand.

Nepal does not even have a definitive figure for the number of LPG cylinders in circulation.

A 2021 certification exercise by Nepal Oil Corporation put the number at about 14.4 million. Industry representatives and distributors, however, estimate that around 17.5 million cylinders are now in the market.

There is also no clear policy governing how many cylinders households, hotels and restaurants should be allowed to hold.

Nor is there an effective system for determining how much gas is needed in each area and allocating supplies accordingly.

That means gas can enter the country in sufficient quantities without reaching consumers at the right time or in the right place.

Where has the system failed?

The current crisis exposes weaknesses at four different levels.

First, cylinder management.

Authorities do not have a reliable count of the cylinders circulating in the market. New cylinders continue to be added, but regulation and monitoring have not kept pace.

Second, distribution.

The reopening of full-cylinder sales caused demand to rise sharply. But supplies were not redistributed quickly enough according to regional demand.

Consumers who have only one cylinder have been particularly vulnerable. When that cylinder runs out, they have no immediate backup and are forced to join queues.

Third, storage.

Nepal consumes roughly 45,000 to 50,000 tonnes of LPG a month.

But industry representatives say the country’s LPG storage capacity, including bulk storage and cylinders at plants, is only around 10,500 tonnes.

Officials at the Ministry of Industry say Nepal needs at least 25,000 tonnes of storage capacity.

The gap leaves the country exposed to even short disruptions in imports or transportation.

Fourth, transportation.

Nepal remains heavily dependent on Indian LPG bullet tankers to bring LPG into the country.

When Indian LPG plants undergo maintenance or transportation is disrupted, Nepal can feel the effects almost immediately.

The current crisis therefore cannot be explained simply by how much gas Nepal imports.

It is a supply-chain problem.

What would fix the problem in the long term?

Making gas available in the market immediately may ease the current queues, but it will not prevent the same problem from returning.

At least four measures are needed.

Build large-scale storage facilities: Stakeholders say Nepal needs infrastructure capable of storing at least 25,000 tonnes of LPG.

Such reserves would allow the country to keep the market supplied for several days even if imports from India were temporarily disrupted.

Build an LPG pipeline: Nepal has long considered reducing its dependence on tanker trucks by building a gas pipeline from Motihari in India to Nepal.

A proposed route from Motihari through the Pathlaiya-Sarlahi area would be about 130 kilometres long.

Indian Oil Corporation has already carried out a route survey and submitted a report, but the project has not moved ahead.

Regulate cylinders: The government needs a clear system determining how many cylinders the market requires, how many cylinders individual consumers should be allowed to hold and how many new cylinders LPG companies can introduce.

Without such controls, the number of cylinders can continue to rise without corresponding improvements in distribution.

Overhaul distribution: Nepal needs a permanent system that allocates LPG according to actual regional demand.

At present, the system appears largely reactive: supplies are redirected only after shortages emerge.

The contradiction at the heart of Nepal's LPG crisis

The government’s message is that there is enough gas.

Industry representatives say imports have increased.

Consumers, meanwhile, are standing in queues because they cannot find a cylinder.

Those three statements can all be true.

The immediate problem is not necessarily the amount of LPG entering Nepal. It is the country’s ability to move, store and distribute that gas efficiently once it arrives.

The shortage has exposed weaknesses in cylinder management, distribution networks, storage capacity and transport infrastructure.

Until those structural problems are addressed, Nepal can continue to have enough gas on paper while consumers struggle to find it in practice.

articles.title: जेनजीको घोषणा : भदौ २३ मा सरकारविरुद्ध देशव्यापी आन्दोलन गर्ने
articles.summary:
कमन जेनजी नेपालले प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह नेतृत्वको सरकारविरुद्ध भदौ २३ गते देशव्यापी आन्दोलन गर्ने घोषणा गरेको छ।

संगठनका अध्यक्ष विकेश साहले मंगलबार जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमार्फत ‘फेक शासनविरुद्ध असल शासन’ नारासहित आन्दोलन गर्ने जनाएका हुन्।

उनले वर्तमान सरकारलाई दमनकारी र जनविरोधी भन्दै जेनजी आन्दोलनका मूल माग सम्बोधन गर्न असफल भएको आरोप लगाए।

साहले जेनजी आन्दोलन केही व्यक्ति वा सरकार परिवर्तनका लागि मात्र नभई समग्र शासन प्रणालीमा आमूल परिवर्तनका लागि भएको दाबी गरेका छन्।

आन्दोलनका क्रममा घाइते तथा सहिद परिवारको उचित सम्बोधन नभएको, किसानका समस्या, मूल्यवृद्धि, मल अभाव र जनजीविकाका सवालमा सरकार उदासीन बनेको उनको आरोप छ।

‘केपी ओलीलाई सडक आन्दोलनबाट फालेझैँ बालेन सरकारलाई पनि सडकबाटै फाल्छौं,’अध्यक्ष साहले चेतावनी दिँदै परिवर्तन चाहने युवा, राजनीतिक दल, नागरिक समाज र राष्ट्रवादी शक्तिलाई आन्दोलनमा सहभागी हुन आह्वान गरेका छन्।

articles.title: अपराधीलाई ‘कोर्रा लगाउनुपर्छ’ भन्ने साम्पाङको अभिव्यक्तिमा विवाद, रेकर्डबाट हटाउन माग
articles.summary:
मंगलबार प्रतिनिधिसभाको बैठकमा श्रम संस्कृति पार्टीका अध्यक्ष तथा सांसद हर्क साम्पाङले दिएको एक अभिव्यक्तिलाई लिएर संसदमा विवाद भएको छ।

उनले देशमा अपराधीहरूलाई नियन्त्रण गर्न ‘फटालाई कर्याक झ्याप गरेर हान्नु, कोरा (कोर्रा) लगाउनुपर्छ’ भन्दै दिएको अभिव्यक्तिप्रति राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) की सांसद इन्दिरा राणाले नियमापत्ति जनाएकी हुन्।

बैठकमा बोल्दै सांसद साम्पाङले देशमा सुरक्षा, न्याय, सेवा-सुविधा र अवसरको कमी रहेको बताउँदै प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहले नैतिक जिम्मेवारी लिनुपर्ने माग गरेका थिए। उनले मस्जिद, मदरसा, गुम्बा र मन्दिरहरूमा आगजनी तथा तोडफोडका घटना बढेको तर सरकार कमजोर बनेको दाबी गरे।

सोही क्रममा उनले भने, ‘मेरो तेरो नभनिकन फटालाई कर्याक झ्याप गरेर हानूँ न कोर्रै कोर्राले, त्यस्तो कानुन बनाऊ, यही हो कानुन बनाउने ठाउँ।’ सांसद साम्पाङको सोही भनाइप्रति आपत्ति जनाउँदै रास्वपा सांसद राणाले नियमापत्ति जनाइन्।

उनले आफू स्वयम् यातना र कोर्रा लगाउने जस्ता कार्यविरुद्ध कानुन बनाउन वर्षौंसम्म वकालत गरेको व्यक्ति भएको स्मरण गराउँदै गरिमामय सदनमा जनता वा अपराधीलाई कोर्रा लगाउने शब्द प्रयोग गर्नु अनुपयुक्त भएको बताइन्।

सांसद राणाले भनिन्, ‘कोर्रा लगाउने, यातना दिने दिनु हुन्न भनेर कानुन ल्याउने व्यक्तिमध्ये म पनि पर्छु। वर्षौँ मैले एडभोकेसी गरेर यो गरिमामय सदनमा कोर्रा जस्तो शब्द आफ्नो जनतालाई, चाहे अपराधी होस् चाहे जे होस्, लगाउने यो शब्द उपयुक्त भएन। यहाँले ती शब्दहरूलाई सुधार्नुपर्छ र यो यस्ता शब्दहरू हाम्रो सदनको रेकर्डबाट हटाउन अनुरोध गर्दछु।’

articles.title: सुर्खेतमा परिचयपत्र देखाएपछि लाइन नबसी ग्यास पाइने
articles.summary:
सुर्खेतमा ज्येष्ठ नागरिक, सुत्केरी र अपाङ्गता भएका व्यक्तिले अब लामो लाइनमा नबसी ग्यास पाउने भएका छन्।

जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय सुर्खेतले उनीहरूको परिचयपत्रका आधारमा ग्यास उपलब्ध गराउने व्यवस्था मिलाएको हो।

ग्यासको अभाव भएपछि पछिल्लो समय सर्वसाधारणले घण्टौँसम्म लाइनमा बस्नुपर्ने अवस्था छ। विशेष गरी ज्येष्ठ नागरिक, सुत्केरी तथा अपाङ्गता भएका व्यक्तिलाई लाइनमा बस्न कठिन हुने भएकाले प्रशासनले उनीहरूका लागि छुट्टै व्यवस्था गरेको हो।

वीरेन्द्रनगरमा ग्यास वितरण गर्ने प्रत्येक सप्लायर्सले वितरण गरिएको दिन १० वटा सिलिन्डर त्यस्ता सेवाग्राहीका लागि छुट्टाउनेछन्। हाल वीरेन्द्रनगरमा दैनिक ६ देखि ८ वटा सप्लायर्सबाट ग्यास वितरण हुने भएकाले प्रशासनको सिफारिसमा दैनिक करिब ६० देखि ८० वटा सिलिन्डर ज्येष्ठ नागरिक, सुत्केरी र अपाङ्गता भएका व्यक्तिलाई उपलब्ध गराइनेछ।

ग्यास लिनका लागि ज्येष्ठ नागरिकले ज्येष्ठ नागरिक परिचयपत्रको प्रतिलिपि, सुत्केरीले अस्पतालबाट जारी भएको दुई महिनाभित्रको सुत्केरी कार्ड र अपाङ्गता भएका व्यक्तिले अपाङ्गता परिचयपत्रको प्रतिलिपि पेस गर्नुपर्नेछ।

ती कागजातका आधारमा जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयले सम्बन्धित ग्यास सप्लायर्सलाई सिफारिस गर्नेछ।

सुर्खेतका निमित्त प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी डिलबहादुर कार्कीका अनुसार सोमबारदेखि नै लाइनमा बस्न कठिन हुने ज्येष्ठ नागरिक, अपाङ्गता भएका व्यक्ति र सुत्केरीका लागि छुट्टाइएको ग्यास प्रशासनको सिफारिसमा उपलब्ध गराउने व्यवस्था सुरु गरिएको हो।

‘लाइनमा बस्न कठिन हुने नागरिकलाई ग्यास लिन सहज होस् भनेर परिचयपत्रका आधारमा सिफारिस गर्ने व्यवस्था मिलाएका छौँ’,कार्कीले भने,‘प्रशासनको यो व्यवस्थाले ग्यासको लाइनमा लामो समय बस्नुपर्ने बाध्यतामा रहेका ज्येष्ठ नागरिक, सुत्केरी र अपाङ्गता भएका व्यक्तिलाई केही राहत पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।’

articles.title: डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्रको दायरा फराकिलो बन्दै
articles.summary:
डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्रको दायरा फराकिलो बन्दै गएको छ। वित्तीय प्रविधि (फिनटेक) र डिजिटल भुक्तानीमा मात्र सीमित नरही कन्टेन्ट क्रिएसन, गिग इकोनोमी, एल्गोरिदमलगायत क्षेत्रमा विस्तारभइ फराकिलो हुँदै गएको विज्ञहरूले बताएका छन्।

राष्ट्रिय सभाअन्तर्गत विकास, आर्थिक मामिला तथा सुशासन समितिद्वारा आयोजित ‘डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्र’ सम्बन्धी छलफलमा विज्ञ रमाकान्त पाण्डेले डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्रको प्रभाव नेपाली बजारमा प्रभावकारी देखिएको बताए।

उनले कन्टेन्ट क्रिएटर र इन्फ्लुएन्सरको गतिविधिले अर्थतन्त्रमा प्रभाव पार्न थालेको उल्लेख गर्दै डिजिटल प्रविधिको विकाससँगै नयाँ प्रकारका व्यवसाय र रोजगारीका क्षेत्र सिर्जना भइरहेको बताए।

‘हिजो हामीले फिनटेक र डिजिटल मनीलाई मात्रै डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्रको रूपमा हेरिरहेका थियौँ, अहिले त्यो संरचनाबाट बाहिर आएका छौँ,’ उनले भने।

विज्ञ दिनेश विष्टले डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्रमा नेपालको भविष्य राम्रो भए पनि डिजिटल पूर्वाधार, फाइभजी नेटवर्क तथा कानुनी संरचनामा सुधार आएको बताए।

उनले डिजिटल सार्वजनिक पूर्वाधार (डिजिटल पब्लिक इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर) निर्माणका लागि आवश्यक कानुनी व्यवस्था गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

‘एउटा विद्यालय वा अस्पतालमा भएको डेटा अर्को निकायले लिन पाउने अधिकार छ कि छैन भन्ने विषयमै स्पष्ट कानुनी व्यवस्था आवश्यक छ,’ विष्टले भने।

‘बैंकले ऋण दिन लालपुर्जा माग्छ। लालपुर्जा भूमि सुधारसम्बन्धी निकायसँग छ भने नागरिकसँग माग्नुको सट्टा सम्बन्धित निकायबाटै विवरण प्राप्त गर्न सक्ने व्यवस्था हुनुपर्छ,’ उनले भने।

उनले कम्पनी दर्ताको उदाहरण दिँदै प्रत्येक वर्ष हजारौँ कम्पनी दर्ता हुने र त्यस क्रममा विभिन्न निकायबीच धेरै चरणमा विवरण प्रमाणीकरण तथा आदानप्रदान गर्नुपर्ने अवस्था रहेको बताए।

डेटा एक्सचेन्ज प्लेटफर्म निर्माण गर्न सके कम्पनी दर्तालगायत सेवामा लाग्ने समय उल्लेख्य रूपमा घटाउन सकिने उन्को भनाइ थियो।

‘डेटा एक्सचेन्ज प्लेटफर्म ल्याउन सक्यौँ भने कम्पनी दर्तामा लाग्ने समय बचत गर्न सकिन्छ,’ उनले भने।

उनले व्यक्तिगत डेटा संरक्षणसम्बन्धी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय अभ्यासको उदाहरण दिँदै नागरिकको व्यक्तिगत विवरण अनधिकृत रूपमा प्रयोग वा चुहावट भएमा सम्बन्धित निकाय जवाफदेही हुने व्यवस्था आवश्यक रहेको बताए।

डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्रको विकासका लागि प्रविधि र पूर्वाधारसँगै डेटा सुरक्षा, अन्तरसरकारी निकायबीच डेटा आदानप्रदान, डिजिटल सुशासन तथा आवश्यक कानुनी संरचनालाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्नुपर्नेमा छलफलका सहभागीले जोड दिएका थिए।
